In HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, the CONNECT method is used to establish a tunnel over a single","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":2,"modality":0,"text":"stream.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":3,"modality":0,"text":"A CONNECT request MUST be constructed as follows:","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":4,"modality":0,"text":"• The :method pseudo-header ﬁeld is set to "CONNECT"","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":5,"modality":0,"text":"• The :scheme and :path pseudo-header ﬁelds are omitted","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":6,"modality":0,"text":"• The :authority pseudo-header ﬁeld contains the host and port to connect to (equivalent to the","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":7,"modality":0,"text":"authority-form ofthe request-target of CONNECT requests; see Section 7.1 of [HTTP]).","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":8,"modality":0,"text":"The request stream remains open at the end ofthe request to carry the data to be transferred. A","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":9,"modality":0,"text":"CONNECT request that does not conform to these restrictions is malformed.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":10,"modality":0,"text":"Bishop Standards Track Page 16","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":11,"modality":0,"text":"RFC 9114 HTTP/3 June 2022","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":12,"modality":0,"text":"A proxy that supports CONNECT establishes a TCP connection ([RFC0793]) to the server identiﬁed","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":13,"modality":0,"text":"in the :authority pseudo-header ﬁeld. Once this connection is successfully established, the proxy","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":14,"modality":0,"text":"sends a HEADERS frame containing a 2xx series status code to the client, as deﬁned in Section","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":15,"modality":0,"text":"15.3 of [HTTP].","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":16,"modality":0,"text":"All DATA frames on the stream correspond to data sent or received on the TCP connection. The","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":17,"modality":0,"text":"payload of any DATA frame sent by the client is transmitted by the proxy to the TCP server; data","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":18,"modality":0,"text":"received from the TCP server is packaged into DATA frames by the proxy. Note that the size and","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":19,"modality":0,"text":"number ofTCP segments is not guaranteed to map predictably to the size and number ofHTTP","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":20,"modality":0,"text":"DATA or QUIC STREAM frames.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":21,"modality":0,"text":"Once the CONNECT method has completed, only DATA frames are permitted to be sent on the","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":22,"modality":0,"text":"stream. Extension frames MAY be used ifspeciﬁcally permitted by the deﬁnition ofthe extension.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":23,"modality":0,"text":"Receipt of any other known frame type MUST be treated as a connection error oftype","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":24,"modality":0,"text":"H3_FRAME_UNEXPECTED.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":25,"modality":0,"text":"The TCP connection can be closed by either peer. When the client ends the request stream (that is,","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":26,"modality":0,"text":"the receive stream at the proxy enters the "Data Recvd" state), the proxy will set the FIN bit on its","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":27,"modality":0,"text":"connection to the TCP server. When the proxy receives a packet with the FIN bit set, it will close","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":28,"modality":0,"text":"the send stream that it sends to the client. TCP connections that remain half closed in a single","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":29,"modality":0,"text":"direction are not invalid, but are often handled poorly by servers, so clients SHOULD NOT close a","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":30,"modality":0,"text":"stream for sending while they still expect to receive data from the target ofthe CONNECT.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":31,"modality":0,"text":"A TCP connection error is signaled by abruptly terminating the stream. A proxy treats any error","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":32,"modality":0,"text":"in the TCP connection, which includes receiving a TCP segment with the RST bit set, as a stream","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":33,"modality":0,"text":"error oftype H3_CONNECT_ERROR.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":34,"modality":0,"text":"Correspondingly, if a proxy detects an error with the stream or the QUIC connection, it MUST close","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":35,"modality":0,"text":"the TCP connection. Ifthe proxy detects that the client has reset the stream or aborted reading","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":36,"modality":0,"text":"from the stream, it MUST close the TCP connection. Ifthe stream is reset or reading is aborted by","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":37,"modality":0,"text":"the client, a proxy SHOULD perform the same operation on the other direction in order to ensure","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":38,"modality":0,"text":"that both directions ofthe stream are cancelled. In all these cases, ifthe underlying TCP","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":39,"modality":0,"text":"implementation permits it, the proxy SHOULD send a TCP segment with the RST bit set.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":40,"modality":0,"text":"Since CONNECT creates a tunnel to an arbitrary server, proxies that support CONNECT SHOULD","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":41,"modality":0,"text":"restrict its use to a set ofknown ports or a list ofsafe request targets; see Section 9.3.6 of [HTTP]","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":42,"modality":0,"text":"for more details.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":43,"modality":0,"text":"4.5. HTTP Upgrade","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":44,"modality":0,"text":"HTTP/3 does not support the HTTP Upgrade mechanism (Section 7.8 of [HTTP]) or the 101","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":45,"modality":0,"text":"(Switching Protocols) informational status code (Section 15.2.2 of [HTTP]).","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":46,"modality":0,"text":"4.6.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":47,"modality":0,"text":"Server Push","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":48,"modality":0,"text":"Bishop Standards Track Page 17","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":49,"modality":0,"text":"RFC 9114 HTTP/3 June 2022","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":50,"modality":0,"text":"Server push is an interaction mode that permits a server to push a request-response exchange to","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":51,"modality":0,"text":"a client in anticipation ofthe client making the indicated request. This trades oﬀnetwork usage","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":52,"modality":0,"text":"against a potential latency gain. HTTP/3 server push is similar to what is described in Section 8.2","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":53,"modality":0,"text":"of [HTTP/2], but it uses diﬀerent mechanisms.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":54,"modality":0,"text":"Each server push is assigned a unique push ID by the server. The push ID is used to refer to the","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":55,"modality":0,"text":"push in various contexts throughout the lifetime ofthe HTTP/3 connection.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":56,"modality":0,"text":"The push ID space begins at zero and ends at a maximum value set by the MAX_PUSH_ID frame.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":57,"modality":0,"text":"In particular, a server is not able to push until after the client sends a MAX_PUSH_ID frame. A","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":58,"modality":0,"text":"client sends MAX_PUSH_ID frames to control the number ofpushes that a server can promise. A","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":59,"modality":0,"text":"server SHOULD use push IDs sequentially, beginning from zero. A client MUST treat receipt of a","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":60,"modality":0,"text":"push stream as a connection error oftype H3_ID_ERROR when no MAX_PUSH_ID frame has been","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":61,"modality":0,"text":"sent or when the stream references a push ID that is greater than the maximum push ID.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":62,"modality":0,"text":"The push ID is used in one or more PUSH_PROMISE frames that carry the control data and header","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":63,"modality":0,"text":"ﬁelds ofthe request message. These frames are sent on the request stream that generated the","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":64,"modality":0,"text":"push. This allows the server push to be associated with a client request. When the same push ID is","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":65,"modality":0,"text":"promised on multiple request streams, the decompressed request ﬁeld sections MUST contain the","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":66,"modality":0,"text":"same ﬁelds in the same order, and both the name and the value in each ﬁeld MUST be identical.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":67,"modality":0,"text":"The push ID is then included with the push stream that ultimately fulﬁlls those promises. The push","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":68,"modality":0,"text":"stream identiﬁes the push ID ofthe promise that it fulﬁlls, then contains a response to the","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":69,"modality":0,"text":"promised request as described in Section 4.1.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":70,"modality":0,"text":"Finally, the push ID can be used in CANCEL_PUSH frames; see Section 7.2.3. Clients use this frame","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":71,"modality":0,"text":"to indicate they do not wish to receive a promised resource. Servers use this frame to indicate","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":72,"modality":0,"text":"they will not be fulﬁlling a previous promise.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":73,"modality":0,"text":"Not all requests can be pushed. A server MAY push requests that have the following properties:","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":74,"modality":0,"text":"• cacheable; see Section 9.2.3 of [HTTP]","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":75,"modality":0,"text":"• safe; see Section 9.2.1 of [HTTP]","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":76,"modality":0,"text":"• does not include request content or a trailer section","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":77,"modality":0,"text":"The server MUST include a value in the :authority pseudo-header ﬁeld for which the server is","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":78,"modality":0,"text":"authoritative. Ifthe client has not yet validated the connection for the origin indicated by the","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":79,"modality":0,"text":"pushed request, it MUST perform the same veriﬁcation process it would do before sending a","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":80,"modality":0,"text":"request for that origin on the connection; see Section 3.3. Ifthis veriﬁcation fails, the client MUST","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":81,"modality":0,"text":"NOT consider the server authoritative for that origin.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":82,"modality":0,"text":"Clients SHOULD send a CANCEL_PUSH frame upon receipt of a PUSH_PROMISE frame carrying a","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":83,"modality":0,"text":"request that is not cacheable, is not known to be safe, that indicates the presence ofrequest","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":84,"modality":0,"text":"content, or for which it does not consider the server authoritative. Any corresponding responses","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":85,"modality":0,"text":"MUST NOT be used or cached.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":86,"modality":0,"text":"Bishop Standards Track Page 18","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":87,"modality":0,"text":"RFC 9114 HTTP/3 June 2022","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":88,"modality":0,"text":"Each pushed response is associated with one or more client requests. The push is associated with","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":89,"modality":0,"text":"the request stream on which the PUSH_PROMISE frame was received. The same server push can","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":90,"modality":0,"text":"be associated with additional client requests using a PUSH_PROMISE frame with the same push ID","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":91,"modality":0,"text":"on multiple request streams. These associations do not aﬀect the operation ofthe protocol, but","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":92,"modality":0,"text":"they MAY be considered by user agents when deciding how to use pushed resources.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":93,"modality":0,"text":"Ordering of a PUSH_PROMISE frame in relation to certain parts ofthe response is important. The","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":94,"modality":0,"text":"server SHOULD send PUSH_PROMISE frames prior to sending HEADERS or DATA frames that","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"ownedIndex":95,"modality":0,"text":"reference the promised responses. This reduces the chance that a client requests a resource that","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}}],"contextOnlyEvidence":[{"contextIndex":0,"modality":0,"text":"the response is malformed (see Section 4.1.2).","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":1,"modality":0,"text":"HTTP/3 does not deﬁne a way to carry the version or reason phrase that is included in an HTTP/","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":2,"modality":0,"text":"1.1 status line. HTTP/3 responses implicitly have a protocol version of "3.0".","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":3,"modality":0,"text":"4.4. The CONNECT Method","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":4,"modality":0,"text":"The CONNECT method requests that the recipient establish a tunnel to the destination origin","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":5,"modality":0,"text":"server identiﬁed by the request-target; see Section 9.3.6 of [HTTP]. It is primarily used with HTTP","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":6,"modality":0,"text":"proxies to establish a TLS session with an origin server for the purposes ofinteracting with "https"","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":7,"modality":0,"text":"resources.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":8,"modality":0,"text":"will be pushed by the server.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":9,"modality":0,"text":"Due to reordering, push stream data can arrive before the corresponding PUSH_PROMISE frame.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":10,"modality":0,"text":"When a client receives a new push stream with an as-yet-unknown push ID, both the associated","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":11,"modality":0,"text":"client request and the pushed request header ﬁelds are unknown. The client can buﬀer the stream","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":12,"modality":0,"text":"data in expectation ofthe matching PUSH_PROMISE. The client can use stream ﬂow control","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":13,"modality":0,"text":"(Section 4.1 of [QUIC-TRANSPORT]) to limit the amount of data a server may commit to the","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":14,"modality":0,"text":"pushed stream. Clients SHOULD abort reading and discard data already read from push streams if","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}},{"contextIndex":15,"modality":0,"text":"no corresponding PUSH_PROMISE frame is processed in a reasonable amount oftime.","facts":{"sourceType":"PDF"}}],"openOrConflictedClaims":[],"retrievedEvidence":[],"layoutEvidence":[],"visualEvidence":[]}}
